/cards/50/title: An Island That Did Not Exist
/cards/50/segments/0/text: At dusk [[NPC1]] waited beside a chipped marble bench. He hoped to recover the trust and jokes of their wandering years. When [[NPC2]] arrived, she first corrected his familiar form of address, then impatiently told him to call her what he liked.
/cards/50/segments/1/text: If you want me back at the {{e_theatre|Theatre}}, say no more. The thought of that place frightens me. So many insults every day. Enough.
/cards/50/segments/2/text: If you were happy with these new friends, I would not ask you to return.
/cards/50/segments/3/text: You dislike my friends? Whom do you propose to replace them with? I want no advice. Forget me.
/cards/50/segments/4/text: He did not understand why she wept and continued describing the theatre's decline. Suddenly she touched his knee, looking as she had many years before.
/cards/50/segments/5/text: Forgive me. {{e_jaime|Jaime}} was ill again this afternoon. He lay there so white, so astonished, and no one could help. One has to think of other things. But returning to act would be useless. The audience wants new farces. There is no point fighting it.
/cards/50/segments/6/text: I was unjust. I was proud and withheld the praise you deserved. You were always a great actress. We could still go to {{e_spain|Spain}}. You would succeed in Madrid.
/cards/50/segments/7/text: The world is the same everywhere.
/cards/50/segments/8/text: Or to an island, where people would love you for yourself.
/cards/50/segments/9/text: Fifty years old, and still dreaming of such islands. They exist only in plays.
/cards/50/segments/10/text: At last she said she was cold and must go. Unable to find words true enough for parting, she bent and kissed his fingers. He remained alone in the thickening cloud, pleased by the gesture and still trying to understand what the conversation had given him.
/cards/51/segments/0/text: I have come again this month. {{e_camila|Camila}}'s politeness grows more complete, so complete that no answer is possible. She does not meet my eyes. I look at the furnishings, thinking that if I stay a little longer, perhaps we will speak of something from the past.
/cards/51/segments/1/text: When conversation fails, I go upstairs to the children. {{e_jaime|Jaime}} is there too. They do not yet require me to change my identity at the door, or prove that my clothes and reputation belong in this house. I stay with them, meet a small need, and the remaining time passes upstairs. At least I can still offer this {{e_care|Care}}.
/cards/51/segments/2/text: On my way back to {{e_lima|Lima}}, people embrace in the streets and take smiling leave of one another. Surely, I think, they draw great comfort from these meetings. We once had that too, without formality or an appointed ten minutes: walking long roads together, speaking whenever something happened.
/cards/51/segments/3/text: I know she has her own life now. Still, I hope that next time she calls me Uncle, her voice might sound a little as it used to. Such a small wish keeps me thinking of next month's visit all the way home. If the children still listen, the long journey seems not entirely wasted.
/cards/52/segments/0/text: News of the smallpox spread through Lima. Hundreds of others were ill, yet the talk and malice gathered around [[NPC1]]. Many secretly hoped that the beauty which had enabled her to leave her former class would finally be damaged. Each rumour from the sickroom seemed to compensate those who rejoiced in her misfortune.
/cards/52/segments/1/text: As soon as she could travel, she left the city for the mountains. She would sell the fine house and gowns, return the {{e_jewels|Jewels}} to their donors. {{e_viceroy|Viceroy Andrés}}, the {{e_archbishop|Archbishop of Lima}} and people who had sincerely liked her still sent enquiries and presents. The messages went unanswered. The presents came back unopened.
/cards/52/segments/2/text: She allowed no one but her nurse and maid to see her. After so many years of admiration, she had bound other people's desire for her company to her face. If they still came now, it must be pity; hidden within their pity, she imagined satisfaction at the reversal.
/cards/52/segments/3/text: She returned more money than she owed. When her anger eased, poverty began to approach. The farm declined. Her children were still there, but her days narrowed to a room she would not leave. She imagined the city's delight and, hearing a footstep, could not tell whether it brought help or another examining gaze.
/cards/52/segments/4/text: {{e_pio|Pio}} did not give up. He watched the children, helped manage the farm and quietly lent her money, eventually gaining admission again. She received him veiled, still speaking sharply. He believed he understood her suffering. Understanding did not mean that every door in the house was therefore open to him.
/cards/53/segments/0/text: Do not bring those things in again. Send them back. Tell them there is no need to enquire. Once I accepted a string of beads and thought it affection. Now the same box on the table makes me wonder only whether its sender has heard about my face.
/cards/53/segments/1/text: This {{e_villa|Camila's Villa}} once seemed a respectable destination. Now every person waiting outside my room makes me want to shut the door more tightly. Perhaps {{e_pio|Pio}} does not think that way. Perhaps he truly means to help. The moment he looks at me, I have already supplied his thoughts.
/cards/53/segments/2/text: I returned the presents, even those I did not have to return. At least I would no longer owe anyone the right to look at me. Only later did I notice how little money remained. A farm does not recover by itself because a door is closed.
/cards/53/segments/3/text: The children are upstairs. {{e_jaime|Jaime}} has always been so frail. I ought to find some help for him, yet every day I have less strength even to leave this room. I refuse pity. I do not know another way to speak my need.
/cards/54/segments/0/text: [[NPC1]] believed she had locked the door. For a brief moment a secret hope returned: after all the methods she had learned onstage, might there be one that could restore something familiar to her face?
/cards/54/segments/1/text: She mixed powder with cream and applied it hurriedly. Once she had laughed at old women at court with faces painted white. Now she faced the {{e_mirror|Dressing Mirror}}, anxious and unwilling to admit that her hope was failing. The colour did not restore the past. It only made her more aware of what she had done.
/cards/54/segments/2/text: Then she saw [[NPC2]] reflected at the door. He had pushed it open and stood there in surprise. She sprang up, covered her face with both hands and screamed. What was unbearable was not simply that he had seen the marks of illness. He had seen her secret wish to conceal them.
/cards/54/segments/3/text: Get out. Never enter my house again. I do not want to see you.
/cards/54/segments/4/text: She followed him into the corridor, hurled things down the stairs and ordered the steward never to admit him to the grounds. The prohibition was clear. For another week he repeatedly tried to see her, then temporarily returned to {{e_lima|Lima}}.
/cards/54/segments/5/text: He could manage accounts, lend money and secure care for the children. He had failed to pause and ask before opening a door. The woman faced the mirror alone again. This time, besides a little secret hope, she had lost the certainty that her door was locked.
/cards/55/segments/0/text: Back in {{e_lima|Lima}}, I found tasks to fill the time. None held me long. Longing makes a fool of a man. At my age I was still like an eighteen-year-old, thinking that one more meeting might allow everything to be explained.
/cards/55/segments/1/text: {{e_camila|Camila}} had forbidden me to enter the grounds. If I knocked as usual, I knew my words would never reach her. I began to devise another way, a voice that would make her come outside herself. I had used ingenuity to enter many doors before. This time I refused to accept her refusal as final.
/cards/55/segments/2/text: I thought of {{e_jaime|Jaime}} too. The child was intelligent and wanted to learn. He should not spend all day among servants and stables. I could teach him, put my house in order and ask {{e_abbess|Mother Pilar}} to find a housekeeper.
/cards/55/segments/3/text: These plans all sounded useful. Thinking of them, I felt I had a reason to climb the mountain road once more. Before dawn, every shutter and door was closed. I stood outside, rehearsing inwardly the voice that did not belong to me.
/cards/56/segments/0/text: [[NPC1]] lay beneath the window, imitating a girl's low sobs. He kept the sound quiet and intermittent for a full quarter of an hour. The faintest blue appeared behind the mountains; grass stirred in the breeze. At last a lamp lit upstairs, the shutter opened, and the veiled [[NPC2]] looked out.
/cards/56/segments/1/text: Who is there? Who is crying?
/cards/56/segments/2/text: Señora, please come down. I am a poor girl called Estrella. Do not send the maid. Come yourself and help me.
/cards/56/segments/3/text: After a pause she agreed. A little later her heavy cloak trailed through the dewy grass. She came round the corner of the house, still keeping her distance.
/cards/56/segments/4/text: Come here to me. Who are you?
/cards/56/segments/5/text: The visitor stood and admitted who he was. The woman who had come to help an unknown girl understood at once that she had been lured outside.
/cards/56/segments/6/text: When will I be rid of you? I want to see no one, speak to no one.
/cards/56/segments/7/text: For the sake of all our years together, grant me one thing. I shall leave and trouble you no more.
/cards/56/segments/8/text: I shall grant nothing. Stay away.
/cards/56/segments/9/text: She went towards a door on the other side. He had to hurry after her to keep within hearing. At last she stopped, tired and angry.
/cards/56/segments/10/text: What is it? Quickly. It is cold, and I am not well yet.
/cards/56/segments/11/text: He asked to take {{e_jaime|Jaime}} to the city for a year and educate him himself. The morning star still shone above. The girl supposedly calling for help did not exist. The person truly drawn into this conversation was a child still asleep inside.
/cards/57/segments/0/text: No. {{e_jaime|Jaime}} is frail, and your house is disorderly. Only the country suits him.
/cards/57/segments/1/text: He has been better these past months. I shall put the house in order, ask {{e_abbess|Mother Pilar}} for a housekeeper and teach him Spanish, Latin, music, everything he ought to know. Only a year.
/cards/57/segments/2/text: A mother cannot part with her child like that. The children and I will manage as best we can. Think no more about me.
/cards/57/segments/3/text: When his request failed, [[NPC2]] abruptly changed his appeal.
/cards/57/segments/4/text: Then repay the money you owe me.
/cards/57/segments/5/text: [[NPC1]] stopped. The poverty she had laboured to conceal was laid bare before her. After a silence her voice became hoarse.
/cards/57/segments/6/text: I have very little money. I shall give you what I have. There are a few {{e_jewels|Jewels}} left; you may have them now. Then we need never see one another again. So you are that hard-hearted. Still, I owe the money and ought to repay it.
/cards/57/segments/7/text: I do not want the money. I only said it to make you grant my request. Let me educate him for a year. I shall love and care for him. Was I a bad teacher before?
/cards/57/segments/8/text: Gratitude, gratitude, always gratitude. You are cruel. I was grateful once—very well. But I am no longer that woman.
/cards/57/segments/9/text: She looked at the stars for a while without agreeing. When she spoke again, another person's wishes finally entered the conversation.
/cards/57/segments/10/text: If the boy wishes to go with you, he may. I shall ask him in the morning. If he wishes it, you will find him at the inn at noon. Good night. God keep you.
/cards/57/segments/11/text: She turned indoors. The demand for repayment had been withdrawn; it could not be treated as though it had never been made. The promise of education still awaited the child's waking answer. She had not surrendered a mother's right to decide forever.
/cards/58/title: We Shall Rest Across the Bridge
/cards/58/segments/0/text: At noon the next day, the solemn little boy arrived at the inn. His once fine clothes were worn and stained. He carried only a small bundle of changes. His mother had given him a gold {{e_coin|Coin}} for spending money and a {{e_stone|Luminous Stone}} to look at in the dark when he could not sleep.
/cards/58/segments/1/text: [[NPC1]] took [[NPC2]] into the cart. Before long he saw that the jolting made the child unwell. He lifted him onto his shoulders and continued. Languages, music and manners—the things he planned to teach—were still waiting in the city. First he must care for a body that could not endure the bouncing wheels.
/cards/58/segments/2/text: Near the valley the boy felt a familiar attack approaching. He wanted to conceal his shame, especially before strangers. Just then they met {{e_captain|Captain Alvarado}}, an acquaintance of the older man. The adults' greetings were ordinary. The child attended only to keeping his face and hands carefully composed.
/cards/58/segments/3/text: Farther on, the older man exchanged words with an elderly woman travelling with a girl: {{e_maria|María}} and {{e_pepita|Pepita}}. Each had arrived by a separate history. For a moment they became a company crossing a river.
/cards/58/segments/4/text: He said they would sit down and rest across the bridge. The child did not have to finish the whole journey, only reach the other side. It was a plain, practical plan of care: find somewhere to sit, let this spell pass, then continue towards the city.
/cards/58/segments/5/text: They did not reach that resting place. The bridge fell into the valley that day. Five lives, previously separate, would thereafter be spoken of under the same date. {{e_juniper|Brother Juniper}} witnessed the moment from before the bridge. Later he would ask whether it was chance or {{e_providence|Providence}}. {{e_letters|Letters}}, memories and contradictory accounts would bring those names before him again.
/cards/59/segments/0/text: {{e_jaime|Jaime}} wishes to go. Now things must be prepared; they cannot remain inside last night's 'if'. The clothes are no longer as fine as before. {{e_pio|Pio}} will see, perhaps others in the city too. I cannot keep the child in this house merely to conceal that.
/cards/59/segments/1/text: A gold {{e_coin|Coin}}, for him to spend himself. And this {{e_stone|Luminous Stone}}: when he cannot sleep, he can look at it in the dark instead of staring only into blackness. I cannot give him a night without pain or fear. I can give him this small thing at hand.
/cards/59/segments/2/text: We agreed on a year. I also remember the cruel words spoken this morning, and why I refuse another demand for gratitude. Entrusting my child to him has not erased those things.
/cards/59/segments/3/text: There is little luggage. Once it is packed, the table is empty again. I remain in this {{e_villa|Camila's Villa}}; no one need keep waiting at the door. Yet when I think of him sleeping in another room tonight, I still want to touch the bundle I have already given away.
